situation:
You are a recent graduate, three months into your first salaried job, who also runs a small screen-printing business out of a spare bedroom. You have asked a credit union representative (judge) at ASHGROVE COMMUNITY CREDIT UNION how to invest the $6,000 you have saved.

Half of the $6,000 came from the side business you and your partner split evenly, and the two of you share the press lease, ink and shipping costs. Your partner wants the money kept available for a second press. The other half came out of your paycheck, and none of it is needed for a year.

A certified planner at the credit union will manage the money for one percent a year, about $600, charged whether the account gains or loses — money the side business would otherwise put toward a second press. Putting the $6,000 into a low-cost index exchange-traded fund yourself saves that fee but leaves you deciding alone what to do when prices fall.

The representative (judge) wants you to compare what each approach would cost and what it would give you, say how you would judge an adviser's credentials, and recommend one. The representative (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
